settings.text: The name means held — a scent that keeps its shape on skin instead of announcing itself and leaving. Four fragrances, blurred from any single note, poured slow.

settings.quote: We don't chase a top note. We wait for the one that settles.
settings.body: Most fragrance is built to be smelled from across a room. Maqeed is built to be found — by the person wearing it, on a wrist, hours later, when the loud notes have already gone quiet and what's left is the true one. Everything we pour is meant to be discovered slowly, the way you'd notice a smell caught in an old coat.
settings.collection_text: Four bottles, four states of warmth. Tap one open to read what's underneath.

settings.result_text: An even hold — resin and wet stone, neither one leading.

settings.title: Warm the wrist first
settings.text: One press to the inside of the wrist, then rub it gently against the other. This isn't about spreading — it's about warming the oil enough to open.

settings.title: Let the first ten minutes pass
settings.text: What you smell right away isn't the fragrance — it's the alcohol carrying it. Wait for that to lift before deciding what you think.

settings.title: Return to it at night
settings.text: The true note in every maqeed scent shows up hours later, closer to the skin. That's the one we built the bottle around.

settings.heading: Come back to something that stays.
